Count detections per animal, time bin and receiver

Source: R/bin_detections.R
bin_detections.Rd

Turns a detection table into the counts that location_surface() reads. For each animal and each time bin in which the animal was detected, the result has one row per receiver listening in the bin: the detections that receiver logged (y, zero for a silent receiver) and the transmissions the animal sent in the bin (n).

Usage

bin_detections(
  detections,
  listening,
  tag_delay,
  bin = "hour",
  codes = NULL,
  min_cover = 0.5
)

Arguments

detections

Detections, one row each, with the columns datetime (POSIXct, UTC), receiver_serial (text), transmitter (text, the tag's code) and animal_id (text, the animal that carried the tag), and optionally station_id. Rows with no animal_id, such as reference tags, are not counted.

listening

Which receivers listened when: receiver-days, deployments, or a list of both (see Details).

tag_delay

Mean delay between transmissions, in seconds (see Details): one number for every transmitter, two numbers giving the shortest and longest delay (their mean is used), or a data frame with the column transmitter and either delay or both min_delay and max_delay (the mean of the two is used). An optional animal_id column lists every code an animal carries, including codes never detected, and an optional codes column sets the rule per transmitter.

bin

Bin length: "hour", "day" or a number of seconds.

codes

How the transmitters of one tag share its transmissions: "shared" or "independent" (see Details). Needed when an animal carries more than one transmitter and tag_delay has no codes column.

min_cover

Share of a bin, from 0 to 1, that a deployment must cover for its receiver to listen in the bin. Not used with receiver-days alone.

Value

A data frame with one row per animal, bin and listening receiver: animal_id, bin_start and bin_end (POSIXct, UTC), receiver_serial, station_id when the listening table has it, y (integer), n

(integer) and listening (logical). Attributes: "bin" (seconds), "n_raised", "swaps_merged", "cover_dropped", "not_listening"

(detections at receivers outside the listening table), "codes" (per animal: transmitters, and the rule when there are two or more) and "rate_check" (per animal: bins, median n, q99_best and ratio, which is NA under 100 bins).

Details

Transmissions. n is the bin length divided by the tag's mean delay between transmissions, rounded to a whole number. The delay is the mean time from the start of one transmission to the start of the next. Where a tag's nominal delay leaves out the transmission itself, a few seconds, add it: otherwise n is a few per cent too high (4% for a 120 s delay and a 5 s transmission), and silent receivers count as slightly stronger evidence than they are. Check how the manufacturer defines the delay. When an animal carries more than one transmitter, codes says how they share the tag's transmissions:

  • "shared": the tag sends one transmission per delay and the codes take turns, so n is the bin length over the mean of the codes' delays. Give each code the tag's delay. In detections of V13AP and V9AP tags most consecutive detections switch code, so their codes take turns. For V16AT tags the evidence is mixed and the rule is unresolved; check them with the rate check below.

  • "independent": each code keeps its own schedule, so n sums the codes' rates.

There is no default for animals with more than one transmitter, because the wrong rule doubles or halves n. Give codes, or a codes column in tag_delay to set it per transmitter.

The floor. A receiver cannot log more transmissions than were sent, so where a receiver logged more detections in a bin than n, n is raised to that count. The number of bins raised is given in a message and in the attribute "n_raised".

Rate check. For each animal with at least 100 detected bins, the attribute "rate_check" gives the 99th percentile of the busiest receiver's count per bin over n. With the right delay and rule it lies near 1; near 0.5 means n is doubled, as when the codes of a tag that takes turns are summed. A warning names animals below 0.6 or above 1.5.

Listening. listening takes one of three forms.

  • Receiver-days: one row per receiver and UTC date on which it listened, with the columns receiver_serial and date (class Date), and optionally station_id and a logical column listening (rows with FALSE are not used). A receiver listens in every bin of a listed date, so with this form a bin must divide a day. The form cannot see the hours of a deployment or recovery day when the receiver was out of the water.

  • Deployments: one row per receiver deployment, with receiver_serial, station_id, deploy_datetime and recover_datetime (NA while deployed). A receiver listens in a bin when its deployment covers at least min_cover of the bin.

  • Both, as list(deployments = , days = ): a receiver listens in a bin when its deployment covers at least min_cover of the bin and the bin's UTC date is a listed day. Use this form when receiver-days mark days that failed a check, so that neither the failed days nor the hours out of the water count as silence.

Receiver-bins left out for covering less than min_cover are counted in the attribute "cover_dropped". At a station, the cover of all its receivers in the bin is summed (at most 1), so a swap within a bin does not drop the station.

Receiver swaps. When the listening table carries station_id and two receivers at one station both listen in a bin, as on the day one replaces the other, the bin keeps one row for the station: the receiver deployed later, with the detections of both. Without this the station would count twice as a silent receiver. The number of merges is in the attribute "swaps_merged".

Detections outside the listening table. A detection at a receiver not listening in its bin keeps a row with listening = FALSE, and a warning gives the count. location_surface() leaves such rows out; add the receiver to the listening table, or lower min_cover, to use them.

Deployments with no serial. Some deployment sheets, such as OTN's simplified ones, give the station but not the receiver's serial. Rows of listening with no receiver_serial but a station_id are then matched to detections by station, when detections has a station_id column: both take the key "station:<station_id>" in receiver_serial, and a message gives the count. Without that column a warning says that those rows cannot be matched. Use a field keyed by station_id with such counts.

Bins are aligned to UTC: hour bins start on the hour and day bins at midnight UTC. Only bins with a detection are returned, so the surfaces describe detected bins.

See also

location_surface(), which reads the result.

Examples

# The Stoney example: five animals, 70 receivers, 48 hours from 1 June 2024.
counts <- bin_detections(stoney_track$detections, stoney_track$receivers,
                         stoney_track$tags)
# One row per animal, hour and listening receiver; y is the count, n the
# transmissions sent in the hour.
head(counts[counts$y > 0, c("animal_id", "bin_start", "station_id", "y", "n")])
#>     animal_id           bin_start station_id  y  n
#> 64  stoney-01 2024-06-01 04:00:00       S064  5 24
#> 134 stoney-01 2024-06-01 05:00:00       S064  7 24
#> 138 stoney-01 2024-06-01 05:00:00       S068 13 24
#> 139 stoney-01 2024-06-01 05:00:00       S069  3 24
#> 204 stoney-01 2024-06-01 06:00:00       S064  6 24
#> 208 stoney-01 2024-06-01 06:00:00       S068  7 24
table(unique(counts[c("animal_id", "bin_start")])$animal_id)  # detected hours
#> 
#> stoney-01 stoney-02 stoney-03 stoney-04 stoney-05 
#>        43        48        44        29        48 

# The same detections by day, with the delay given as the shortest and
# longest delay in seconds.
daily <- bin_detections(stoney_track$detections, stoney_track$receivers,
                        tag_delay = c(120, 180), bin = "day")
daily[daily$y > 0, c("animal_id", "bin_start", "station_id", "y", "n")][1:5, ]
#>    animal_id  bin_start station_id  y   n
#> 63 stoney-01 2024-06-01       S063  2 576
#> 64 stoney-01 2024-06-01       S064 82 576
#> 65 stoney-01 2024-06-01       S065 24 576
#> 67 stoney-01 2024-06-01       S067  8 576
#> 68 stoney-01 2024-06-01       S068 75 576
